data.narrative:
Orqa is a Series A drone and autonomous systems company that has raised approximately $22M to date. The comparable universe in Drones & Autonomous comprises eight private companies, including Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and Elroy Air, alongside zero public peers. The absence of public comparables and insufficient same-stage private peers limits traditional peer benchmarking.

Given data constraints, valuation relies on stage-progression methodology. Applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to Series B transitions to the $22M total raised proxy yields $44M. This represents the median point in the triangulated range. The low and high bounds—$37M and $51M respectively—reflect reasonable variance around this central estimate, accounting for execution risk and market conditions in an early-stage, capital-intensive sector.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $37M to $51M, with $44M as the midpoint. Key uncertainties include the inability to apply peer-median methodology due to insufficient comparable data at matching stage and tier, the reliance on a single methodological pillar, and inherent stage-specific execution risk in autonomous systems development. More granular data on product traction, team track record, and market adoption would strengthen conviction in any point estimate within this range.
